newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end weaker on corrective sales.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end weaker on corrective sales.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed slightly lower on Thursday due to profit-taking after the previous day's sharp advance in the key average by more than three percent.

Brokers said investors were prompted to secure temporary profits as the dollar briefly dipped below 116.00 yen. The yen's strength against the dollar fuels worries that it may hurt Japanese exporters' profits.
The 225-share Nikkei average lost 39.11 points or 0.19 percent to finish at 20,312.23. June Nikkei futures fell 90 points to 20,310.

There was no direct impact from Japan's industrial output data for April released earlier in the afternoon, but brokers said they would pay close attention to the currency and interest rate markets, which were affected by the outcome.
Japan's industrial production in April fell a preliminary 0.4 percent from the previous month on a seasonally adjusted basis, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said.
